newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM asks nation to cast out corruption.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM asks nation to cast out corruption.

text.p: India Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, addressing the nation on its 50th anniversary of independence, appealed to citizens to stamp out corruption which he said was threatening the country.

"Let us all resolve today that we would not give a single penny as a bribe to get our work done at any level," Gujral said in a nationally televised address from the ramparts of the 17th century Red Fort in the capital.
Echoing President K.R. Narayanan who had earlier addressed the nation in a solemn midnight speech, Gujral called for a mass movement to excommunicate the corrupt, whom he called traitors.

Gujral, who heads a four-month-old centre-left coalition government, reiterated that India would not sign a global treaty banning nuclear weapons tests unless the declared nuclear powers pledged to destroy their arsenals.

He said India wanted better relations with arch-rival Pakistan, which celebrated its half-century of independence on Thursday, but closer ties would be possible only if there was no external interference in India's affairs.

The prime minister announced a special fund for girls in poor families, and said doctors should be banned by law from disclosing whether a foetus is a boy or girl. Social planners say many Indian families discriminate against girls for economic reasons.
